topic: ICSE 10th Board Section A - General Pattern & MCQs (20 Marks)

questions.question: What type of data structures are Arrays and Classes considered?
questions.explanation: A data type that represents a number of similar or different data under a single declaration is called a composite data type (or non-primitive type)[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which Wrapper Class corresponds to the primitive type 'char'?
questions.explanation: The Java wrapper class explicitly designated for the primitive data type 'char' is 'Character'[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which math function is utilized to compute exponents (base raised to a power)?
questions.explanation: The Math.pow() function handles exponentiation, accurately taking two parameters: base and power[cite: 1].

questions.question: What is the technical description of 'Unboxing' in Java?
options: Converting an object to an array
Converting wrapper class objects into primitive data types
Typecasting a double to an int
questions.answer: Converting wrapper class objects into primitive data types
questions.explanation: Unboxing is the system of converting an object of a wrapper class completely into primitive data type[cite: 1].

questions.question: What is an absolute necessity before utilizing Binary Search on an array?
options: Array must be sorted in an order
questions.answer: Array must be sorted in an order
questions.explanation: Binary search technique can be used exclusively when the array elements are completely sorted in an order[cite: 1].

questions.question: What happens if a method is strictly defined with a return type of 'void'?
options: It performs actions but does not return any output value
questions.answer: It performs actions but does not return any output value
questions.explanation: A procedural function defined with the return type void fundamentally performs some actions but definitively does not return any output value[cite: 1].

questions.question: What precisely does the compareTo() string method calculate to determine output?
questions.explanation: The compareTo() method calculates and returns an integer representing the exact ASCII difference between the two strings[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which of the following method signatures successfully overloads 'void obj(int a, double b)'?
questions.explanation: Function overloading can be effortlessly implemented by rearranging or altering the strict order of parameters within two identically named methods[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which String method deletes whitespace from both endpoints of the text?
questions.explanation: The trim() function aggressively removes all white/blank spaces situated at the beginning as well as the end of a string[cite: 2].

questions.question: What operates as the system-enforced default value for all standalone boolean variables?
questions.explanation: In standard Java protocol, uninitialized boolean fields natively default to false[cite: 2].

questions.question: Which specific method generates a new string by extracting characters from an existing string?
questions.explanation: The substring() method returns the extracted sequence securely starting from the designated initial index[cite: 2].

questions.question: Which specific keyword commands dynamic memory allocation for newly instantiated arrays?
questions.explanation: The keyword 'new' natively commands the compiler to allocate dynamic block space specifically tailored for data storage operations[cite: 2].

questions.question: Are Java Strings capable of being internally modified after creation?
questions.explanation: In Java architecture, standard String objects firmly remain immutable, signaling that their internal state decisively cannot be modified posthumously[cite: 2].

questions.question: What is the technical terminology for the data values actually transmitted to a method during invocation?
questions.explanation: The raw values that are functionally dispatched to the method directly during its call operation are globally recognized as 'Actual parameters'[cite: 2].

questions.question: Which of these accurately outlines a key feature of a Pure Function (Accessor)?
options: It forcefully changes the state of an object
It does not cause any internal change in the state of an object
questions.answer: It does not cause any internal change in the state of an object
questions.explanation: A pure function, upon invocation, safely maintains data integrity by ensuring zero internal change registers in the foundational state of an object[cite: 2].

questions.question: During a Binary Search algorithm, what exact mathematical formula reliably determines the middle index marker?
questions.explanation: The algorithmic process routinely demands calculating the central pivot precisely via (First + Last) / 2[cite: 2].

questions.question: Which of the following represents an exit-controlled loop in Java?
questions.explanation: A do-while loop evaluates its testing condition after executing the loop body at least once, making it strictly exit-controlled.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to refer directly to the current invoking object within an instance method?
questions.explanation: The 'this' keyword acts as a reference to the current object whose method or constructor is being invoked.

questions.question: What is the return type of the comparison expression (10 > 5 && 4 < 2)?
questions.explanation: Logical operators combined with relational operators always evaluate to a primitive boolean value (true or false).

questions.question: Which package is automatically imported by default into every Java compilation unit?
questions.explanation: The java.lang package contains core classes (such as System, String, and Math) and is automatically imported into every Java program without explicit import statements.
